question: In Turner syndrome, echocardiography alone is sufficient cardiac screening — a cardiac MRI is not routinely needed.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Cardiac MRI is mandatory in Turner syndrome in addition to echocardiography, because echo does not reliably visualise the aortic arch. Aortic coarctation and bicuspid aortic valve occur in 30–50% of cases and carry risk of aortic dissection.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — echocardiography ALONE is NOT sufficient. Cardiac MRI is also required because echo can miss aortic arch anomalies (bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation) that are present in up to 30–50% of Turner syndrome patients.
